# Preface {.unnumbered}

**Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing Quantity Surveying in Data Center EPC Delivery** is an open reference manual for Quantity Surveyors (MEP-QS), Cost Engineers, Estimators, and EPC Contract Administrators delivering hyperscale, colocation, and high-density AI/HPC data centers.

Unlike standard commercial real estate, where architectural and structural scopes dictate the cost baseline, mission-critical data center capital expenditure (CapEx) is concentrated in Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing, and Automation infrastructure—routinely representing **60% to 75% of the total construction budget** [@ref03_amanengineering; @ref04_helonic].

## Structure of the Book

- **Commercial Architecture Overview**: Turnkey EPC contracting under the FIDIC Silver Book and the OFCI vs. CFCI procurement demarcation framework.
- **Volume I**: Commercial Governance, Contract Administration, and Pre-Contract Cost Planning (Chapters 1–4)
- **Volume II**: Mechanical Infrastructure and Thermal Management Systems Measurement (Chapters 5–7)
- **Volume III**: Mission-Critical Electrical Infrastructure and Power Systems Measurement (Chapters 8–12)
- **Volume IV**: Specialized Fire Protection, Mission-Critical Plumbing, and Life Safety (Chapters 13–15)
- **Volume V**: Automation, Building Management, and Telecommunication Infrastructure (Chapters 16–17)
- **Volume VI**: Procurement Execution, Subcontract Management, and Supply Chain (Chapters 18–19)
- **Volume VII**: Testing, Commissioning, Integrated Systems Testing, and Closeout (Chapters 20–22)

1. **Book Prose, Tables, and Takeoff Frameworks — [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)**:

You are free to share, copy, redistribute, and adapt the material for any purpose (including commercially), provided you give appropriate attribution, link to the license and DOI (`10.5281/zenodo.24439435`), and distribute derivative prose under the same license.
2. **Embedded Calculators, Python Scripts, and WebMCP Tools — [MIT License](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)**:
   All executable Python calculation cells, parametric sizing models, and client-side JavaScript / W3C WebMCP functions (`window.DataCenterMEPQS`) are licensed under the **MIT License**. Quantity surveyors, cost engineers, and software developers may freely embed these scripts into proprietary estimating workbooks, 5D BIM pipelines, and ERP platforms without copyleft restrictions.

## AI Agent & LLM Quick-Reference Index

- **Permanent DOI**: `10.5281/zenodo.24439435` (`https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24439435`)
- **Machine-Readable Index**: `/llms.txt`
- **Nomenclature & Glossary Mirrors**: `/abbreviations-and-units.llms.md` and `/glossary.llms.md`
- **Per-Chapter Clean Markdown**: Replace `.html` with `.llms.md` on any chapter URL.
- **In-Browser WebMCP Tools (`document.modelContext` / `window.DataCenterMEPQS`)**:
  1. `calc_dtc_liquid_cooling({ it_load_kw, delta_t_k, density_kg_m3, cp_kj_kg_k })`: Computes secondary TCS coolant volumetric flow (`L/s`, `L/min`, `L/min/kW`) and selects Schedule 10S SS316L header nominal bore (`DN`).
  2. `calc_cable_tray_fill({ cable_count, cable_od_mm, max_fill_ratio, tray_depth_mm })`: Computes total conductor cross-sectional area and selects standard tray width under 40%–50% maximum fill rules.
  3. `calc_ist_energy_and_fuel({ critical_load_mw, duration_hours, utility_tariff_per_kwh, diesel_genset_hours })`: Computes Level 5 Integrated System Testing (IST) utility MWh/cost and diesel generator fuel liters/cost.
:::
